metadata.title: Logarithmic Oscillatory Dark Energy: Full-Covariance Pantheon+ SNe Ia, DESI Year 1 BAO, and Planck CMB Constraints with ESA Euclid Forecasts (v2.0)
metadata.description: Revised Version 2.0. We investigate a bounded, scale-invariant logarithmic harmonic dark energy equation of state, w(a) = -1 + A sin((2*pi/lambda) ln(a) + phi_0), with an exact analytical solution to the relativistic continuity equation. Replacing the diagonal-only supernova approximation of Version 1.0, we implement an exact joint likelihood combining: (1) the uncalibrated Pantheon+ Hubble-flow SNe Ia sample (N = 1,580) with the full 1580x1580 STAT+SYS covariance matrix analytically marginalized over the absolute magnitude offset M; (2) DESI Year 1 BAO measurements (12 observables across 7 redshift bins, 0.295 <= z <= 2.330); and (3) the Planck 2018 CMB shift parameter R(z_* = 1089.92) = 1.7502 +/- 0.0046. We show that Pantheon+ SNe Ia alone with full covariance recover Om = 0.3325 +/- 0.0182 for flat LCDM (chi2/dof = 0.879) and show no preference for dynamical dark energy (Delta chi2 = -0.49), proving that the Delta chi2 ~ -11 in v1 arose from neglecting off-diagonal calibration covariances. Combining Pantheon+ + DESI BAO + Planck CMB yields an interior best fit (zero boundary collisions) with Delta chi2 = -3.75 for CPL (w0 = -0.867, wa = -0.547) and Delta chi2 = -3.90 for Log-Oscillatory (A = 0.218, lambda = 3.09, phi0 = 0.592 rad; Delta AIC = +2.10, Delta BIC = +18.22). Full emcee MCMC posteriors are propagated into the ESA Euclid spectroscopic BAO window (0.9 < z < 1.8).
